summary: Sprint-2 ExpenseSync backend tested. 27/27 pytest cases pass covering: budgets CRUD (create, idempotent-per-category update, 400 on non-positive limit, list, delete), dashboard new fields (budgets[] with spent/pct/over_budget/near_limit + recurring_count; over_budget=True at exact boundary spent==limit; duplicates excluded from spent), analytics/monthly-trend (6-month series in oldest→newest order with month/label/amount, missing months=0, sum of debits excluding duplicates & credits, months param clamped to 1..12), analytics/recurring (>=2 distinct months in last 4 months within ±15% avg; excludes single-month, high-variance, credits, and duplicates; dashboard.recurring_count matches len(items); total_monthly = sum(avg_amount); category and last_seen populated), and auth enforcement (401 without bearer and with bad bearer) on all new endpoints. Verified no MongoDB _id leaked on /api/budgets, /api/analytics/*, and dashboard.budgets subtree. Sprint-1 tests were not re-run per instructions.

minor.issue: Month-stepping uses `cursor - timedelta(days=1)` then `.replace(day=1)` in a loop. Works for the common case, but if the current-month datetime ever lands on very early hours combined with DST/edge dates it is fragile. Consider using calendar-aware math (e.g. dateutil.relativedelta(months=1)). Cosmetic; all 6-month/12-month orderings verified correct.

Fuzzy merchant matching uses only the first significant token via `_merchant_key`; the returned `merchant` field is whichever raw string was on the latest txn. If a user has two variants (e.g. 'NETFLIX' and 'Netflix India'), the response returns only one label — fine for now but worth documenting in UI.

Uses HTTP 200 on both create and update. Not strictly wrong for an upsert endpoint (mirrors the spec's 'idempotent per category (updates limit)'), but 201-on-create / 200-on-update would be more conventional if wanted.

action_items: None required — sprint-2 acceptance criteria fully met. Optionally: switch monthly-trend stepping to `dateutil.relativedelta(months=1)` for calendar correctness, and consider 201 status on new budget creation.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 695 lines (was 522 in sprint-1). Very close to the 700-line soft limit; the next feature should trigger a split (auth.py, parser.py, transactions.py, dashboard.py, budgets.py, analytics.py).

`/api/dashboard` recomputes recurring on every call by scanning up to 5000 debit txns from the last ~4 months and doing amount-variance math in Python. Fine at current volumes but worth an aggregation pipeline / cached view when txn count grows.

`_detect_recurring` catches its outer exception in `/api/dashboard` and silently returns 0 recurring — good for resilience but currently masks any real bug. Consider logging the exception in the except branch.

`analytics_recurring` computes `total_monthly = sum(avg_amount)` which is a decent proxy for 'monthly commitment' but is not truly monthly (e.g. a merchant seen in 2 of last 4 months still contributes full avg). Fine per spec — flagging for future refinement.

Both new POST endpoints return the raw stored dict without an explicit response_model. Works because `find_one({...},{'_id':0})` strips `_id` and the Pydantic Budget is dict()-serialized, but a `response_model=Budget` would tighten the API contract.
seed_data_creation: Tests insert their own controlled debit/credit txns directly into MongoDB via the shared TEST_USER_ID (user_test000001) using a `fresh` fixture that wipes both `transactions` and `budgets` collections before AND after each test. No global seed pollution. Recurring tests seed same-merchant debits across multiple months (days_ago 2/35/70).
